investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~149 s before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration issue localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Three independent pod attempts across ~7 minutes all hit the same wall, strongly suggesting sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded from scheduling by the pod's affinity/selector rules. If those rules are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, the effective scheduling pool is reduced to only 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortage.

[Possible] Peer-pod VM quota limit reached at the infrastructure or cloud provider level: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is typically backed by a cloud VM quota; if the quota ceiling was hit, no new VMs can be provisioned regardless of node count.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying all available VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes.

[Lower likelihood] Node affinity rules targeting a node pool that was scaled down or cordoned: if the 2 kata-capable nodes were recently drained or had their capacity reduced, the effective VM slot count would drop to zero.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not schedule a VM-backed pod, the probe never reached the state-polling step and returned zero evidence, violating the required-evidence contract for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two eligible nodes. With 0/6 nodes schedulable — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1905), which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot. Because no slot is available and preemption found no victims, the pod remains pending until the eval times out (~142–149 seconds), and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.

This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents agent VM creation entirely. The eval failure is a direct consequence of this scheduling blockage; no eval evidence was produced because the pod never started. This is an eval-observed infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-facing production outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state within the eval timeout window.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~149 s before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract-gap failure. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity or configuration issue localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]; neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new pods. Three independent pod attempts across ~7 minutes all hit the same wall, strongly suggesting sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity or node selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded from scheduling by the pod's affinity/selector rules. If those rules are overly restrictive or if node labels changed, the effective scheduling pool is reduced to only 2 nodes, amplifying the impact of any capacity shortage.

[Possible] Peer-pod VM quota limit reached at the infrastructure or cloud provider level: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is typically backed by a cloud VM quota; if the quota ceiling was hit, no new VMs can be provisioned regardless of node count.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents that were not cleaned up may be occupying all available VM slots on the 2 eligible nodes.

[Lower likelihood] Node affinity rules targeting a node pool that was scaled down or cordoned: if the 2 kata-capable nodes were recently drained or had their capacity reduced, the effective VM slot count would drop to zero.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not schedule a VM-backed pod, the probe never reached the state-polling step and returned zero evidence, violating the required-evidence contract for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two eligible nodes. With 0/6 nodes schedulable — 2 due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1905), which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot. Because no slot is available and preemption found no victims, the pod remains pending until the eval times out (~142–149 seconds), and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted across the 2 eligible nodes (0/6 nodes available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector), and preemption is not viable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents agent VM creation entirely. The eval failure is a direct consequence of this scheduling blockage; no eval evidence was produced because the pod never started. This is an eval-observed infrastructure condition, not a confirmed user-facing production outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new remote agent pods, and preemption found no victims to evict.

[Likely contributing] Only 2 of 6 cluster nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and match the pod's node affinity/selector; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible. This small eligible-node pool means any concurrent or leaked agent pods can saturate capacity quickly.

[Possible] A prior eval run or user workload left one or more remote agent pods running and not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner is designed to handle this, but a prior crash or timeout could leave orphaned pods consuming the vm resource slots).
[Possible] The kata-peerpods node pool was scaled down or a node became NotReady, reducing available vm slots below the minimum needed to schedule new pods.

[Lower likelihood] The pod's node affinity or selector was recently changed in a way that further restricts eligible nodes, but no suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this hypothesis.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on all 6 cluster nodes to confirm current capacity and allocation — this is the most direct way to verify the exhaustion diagnosis.
List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, including any orphaned pods from prior eval runs, and terminate any that are no longer needed to free capacity.
If capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate scaling the kata-peerpods node pool to add more nodes carrying the vm resource.
Review the withCleanup mechanism in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure it reliably terminates agent pods even when the eval times out or errors, to prevent future slot leakage.
Monitor whether the failure recurs across subsequent scheduled eval runs — if it does, the capacity problem is sustained and requires infrastructure remediation rather than a one-time cleanup.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 185), so this check alone does not trigger a feature outage classification; however, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183-184) and also failed, which may affect the feature's degraded/outage status per the degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource shows available capacity on the eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and another cause (e.g., node affinity misconfiguration) would need to be primary.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime check rather than a shared scheduling constraint.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload briefly exhausted capacity) rather than a sustained capacity problem.

If the cluster node count or kata-peerpods node pool configuration shows more than 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, the '2 Insufficient' count in the scheduler message would need re-examination.
If orphaned pods from prior eval runs are not present on the cluster, the leaked-pod hypothesis is disproved and the cause is pure capacity exhaustion or node pool scaling.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the minimum number of nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource are Ready, alerting before capacity is fully exhausted.
Consider a dedicated eval that measures the time-to-schedule for remote agent pods as a leading indicator of capacity pressure, with a warning threshold before full exhaustion occurs.
